newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Low quantities keep Colombo rubber prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Low quantities keep Colombo rubber prices firm.

text.p: Rubber prices were stable at the Colombo auction as buyers scrambled for a limited supply of latex, which was reduced in quality by rain, brokers said on Thursday.
"Buyers are short because quantities are not coming into the market," said Lanil Waniganayake of exporter Almar Trading Company.
"The market is holding because people are buying whatever is available," he said.

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, fetched 87.50 rupees ($1.50) per kg, compared with 87.65 rupees per kg last week. Number one dropped slightly to 86 rupees from 86.25 last week, while RSS 1 went unquoted, according to brokerage John Keells.
On offer was 135 tonnes, about half the quantity usually sold through the Colombo auction.
Rain, which hampers rubber tapping, in the longer term also reduces latex quality, they said. ($1=58.70)
